query: SELECT * FROM duckdb_functions() WHERE database_name='bson' ORDER BY schema_name,function_name
rows: Split a concatenated length-prefixed BSON stream into one row per document

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Split a `BLOB` holding N concatenated length-prefixed BSON documents (each is `int32 length ++ body ++ 0x00`) into one row per document: columns idx (`BIGINT`, zero-based position) and doc (`BLOB`, the single document's bytes). This is exactly the wire shape of a mongodump `.bson` file body, an oplog batch, or a GridFS reassembly. Stops cleanly at the first malformed length prefix — partial trailing bytes are ignored (never panics). Feed `doc` to decode / to_json / field. Use as a LATERAL table function over a column of concatenated-BSON blobs.
rows.vgi.doc_md: LATERAL: fan a concatenated length-prefixed BSON stream into rows of `(idx BIGINT, doc BLOB)`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Split two concatenated empty documents.","sql":"SELECT idx, octet_length(doc) AS n FROM bson.main.bson_seq(from_hex('05000000000500000000')) ORDER BY idx"}]
rows.vgi.title: BSON Sequence Split

rows: Decode a BSON document to its richest form (Extended JSON in v1)

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Decode a BSON document to its richest self-describing form and return it as text. `decode(doc)` is the zero-decisions codec: it always yields canonical MongoDB Extended JSON v2 — the lossless column that preserves ObjectId, Decimal128, `UUID`, and the Timestamp-vs-UTCDateTime distinction — and is exactly equivalent to `to_json(doc, 'canonical')`. Prefer `to_json` when you want to choose canonical vs relaxed rendering; reach for `decode` when you just want one stable lossless column and no mode decision. The optional `mode` ('auto', 'struct', 'map', 'json') is a forward-looking hint for the output shape you would like, but because a DuckDB scalar fixes its output column type at bind time with no data sample, all four currently materialize as the same canonical Extended JSON text — the argument does not yet change the result, so omit it unless you are signalling intent. For a typed projection of a known shape, cast the JSON or use `field(doc, path, as)` per leaf. Returns NULL for a malformed blob.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Decode BSON to its richest self-describing form → canonical Extended JSON (the stable lossless column). Equivalent to `to_json(doc, 'canonical')`; prefer `to_json` when you need the canonical/relaxed choice. `mode` ∈ {auto, struct, map, json} is a forward-looking shape hint that currently always returns the same Extended JSON text.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Decode forcing JSON mode.","sql":"SELECT bson.main.decode(bson.main.from_json('{\"a\":1}'), 'json') AS d"}]
rows.vgi.title: BSON Decode

rows: Encode a DuckDB STRUCT/MAP value as a BSON document

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Encode a DuckDB value as a BSON document. `STRUCT` → embedded document; `MAP` → document; `LIST` → array; `TIMESTAMP`/`TIMESTAMPTZ` → UTCDateTime; `UUID` → Binary subtype 0x04; `BLOB` → Binary subtype 0x00; integers → Int32/Int64 by range; `DOUBLE` → Double; `DECIMAL` → Decimal128. The top-level value MUST be a document (a `STRUCT` or `MAP`) — BSON has no top-level scalar, so a bare scalar raises an error. Returns NULL for a NULL input.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Encode a DuckDB `STRUCT`/`MAP` as BSON document bytes. The inverse of `decode` / the typed companion of `from_json`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Encode a struct to BSON and hex it.","sql":"SELECT to_hex(bson.main.encode({'a': 1, 'b': 'x'})) AS h"}]
rows.vgi.title: BSON Encode

rows: Extract a BSON field by dotted path (inferred leaf rendering)

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Extract one field from a BSON document by dotted path ('o._id', 'items.0.sku') without materializing the whole document, returning a `VARCHAR`. The optional `as` argument coerces the leaf to a cast-ready string: 'objectid' → 24-hex, 'decimal' → the canonical decimal literal (cast with `::DECIMAL(38,4)`), 'uuid' → canonical `UUID` (cast with `::UUID`), 'datetime'/'timestamp' → RFC 3339 (cast with `::TIMESTAMPTZ`), 'blob' → lowercase hex, 'json' → canonical Extended JSON. With no `as` (or NULL), the leaf is inferred (scalars render bare). A missing path → NULL. Lossless typed projection a naive JSON path would corrupt.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Extract a field by dotted path → `VARCHAR`. `as` ∈ {objectid, decimal, uuid, timestamp, datetime, blob, json} coerces the leaf to a cast-ready string; NULL infers.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Extract _id as a hex ObjectId.","sql":"SELECT bson.main.field(bson.main.from_json('{\"_id\":{\"$oid\":\"54759eb3c090d83494e2d804\"}}'), '_id', 'objectid') AS id"}]
rows.vgi.title: BSON Field Extract

rows: Encode an Extended JSON v2 string as BSON document bytes

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Parse a MongoDB Extended JSON v2 string (canonical OR relaxed) into BSON document bytes. Interprets the typed wrappers ({"$oid":…}, {"$numberDecimal":…}, {"$date":…}, {"$binary":…}, {"$timestamp":…}, …). Round-trips decode∘encode∘to_json('canonical') to byte-identity on canonical inputs. Returns NULL on invalid JSON or a non-document top-level value.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Encode Extended JSON v2 text as BSON document bytes. Inverse of `to_json`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Encode a JSON document to BSON and hex it.","sql":"SELECT to_hex(bson.main.from_json('{\"a\":1}')) AS h"}]
rows.vgi.title: Extended JSON → BSON

rows: Return true iff the blob is exactly one well-formed BSON document

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Return TRUE iff the blob is exactly one well-formed BSON document per the BSON spec (declared length matches the bytes, types known, cstrings NUL-terminated, valid UTF-8, no trailing bytes). A cheap structural pass — it never allocates a value tree. Never errors or panics: a malformed/hostile blob simply returns FALSE; a NULL input returns NULL. See `well_formed` for the failure reason.
rows.vgi.doc_md: TRUE iff the blob is one well-formed BSON document. Total (never throws). See `well_formed` for the reason on failure.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Validate a tiny empty BSON document (05 00 00 00 00).","sql":"SELECT bson.main.is_valid(from_hex('0500000000')) AS ok"}]
rows.vgi.title: BSON Is-Valid

rows: List the top-level field names of a BSON document in document order

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Return the top-level field names of a BSON document as a `LIST<VARCHAR>`, in document order (BSON preserves insertion order). Use it to discover the shape of a collection's documents or to drive dynamic projection. Returns NULL for a malformed blob.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Top-level field names → `LIST<VARCHAR>` in document order.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"List the keys of a {a:1,b:2} document.","sql":"SELECT bson.main.keys(bson.main.from_json('{\"a\":1,\"b\":2}')) AS k"}]
rows.vgi.title: BSON Keys

rows: Read a glob of mongodump `.bson` files into one row per document

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Read a glob of mongodump `.bson` files (each a concatenation of length-prefixed BSON documents) and fan them into one row per document: columns idx (`BIGINT`, per-file zero-based position), doc (`BLOB`, one document), and file (`VARCHAR`, the source path). Point it at a backup directory (e.g. '/backups/mydb/*.bson') to get every document joinable in SQL, then feed `doc` to decode / to_json / field. Stops cleanly at any trailing partial document. v1 reads local-filesystem globs; for cloud dumps use read_blob('s3://…/*.bson') + bson_seq(content). The worker opens no sockets of its own.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Read a glob of mongodump `.bson` files into rows of `(idx BIGINT, doc BLOB, file VARCHAR)`. Local filesystem in v1.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Count the documents per file in a committed mongodump .bson fixture.","sql":"SELECT file, count(*) AS docs FROM bson.main.mongodump_read('test/data/users.bson') GROUP BY file ORDER BY file"}]
rows.vgi.title: Read mongodump .bson Files

rows: Convert a 24-char hex ObjectId string to its 12-byte BLOB

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Convert a 24-char hexadecimal ObjectId string to its 12-byte `BLOB` form. Returns NULL for a string that is not a valid 24-char ObjectId. The inverse of objectid_hex.
rows.vgi.doc_md: 24-char hex `VARCHAR` → 12-byte ObjectId `BLOB`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"12-byte ObjectId from hex.","sql":"SELECT to_hex(bson.main.objectid_from_hex('54759eb3c090d83494e2d804')) AS b"}]
rows.vgi.title: Parse an ObjectId Hex String to Bytes

rows: Convert a 12-byte ObjectId BLOB to its 24-char hex string

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Convert a 12-byte ObjectId `BLOB` to its 24-char lowercase hexadecimal string. Returns NULL when the input is not exactly 12 bytes. The inverse of objectid_from_hex.
rows.vgi.doc_md: 12-byte ObjectId `BLOB` → 24-char hex `VARCHAR`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Hex of a 12-byte ObjectId.","sql":"SELECT bson.main.objectid_hex(bson.main.objectid_from_hex('54759eb3c090d83494e2d804')) AS h"}]
rows.vgi.title: ObjectId to Hex

rows: Return the creation time embedded in an ObjectId (TIMESTAMPTZ)

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Return the creation time embedded in an ObjectId as a `TIMESTAMPTZ` — the first 4 bytes of every ObjectId are the seconds since the Unix epoch. Accepts either a 24-char hex `VARCHAR` or a 12-byte `BLOB`. This is the cheap "when was this document first written" probe — no separate createdAt field needed. Returns NULL for a value that is not a valid ObjectId.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Creation time embedded in an ObjectId → `TIMESTAMPTZ`. Accepts 24-hex `VARCHAR` or 12-byte `BLOB`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Creation time of an ObjectId.","sql":"SELECT bson.main.objectid_timestamp('54759eb3c090d83494e2d804') AS created"}]
rows.vgi.title: ObjectId Embedded Timestamp

rows: Return the raw (time, increment) pair of a BSON Timestamp as STRUCT(t,i)

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Normalize a BSON internal Timestamp to `STRUCT(t UINTEGER, i UINTEGER)` — the raw (time-in-seconds, increment) pair of the 0x11 replication clock. `t` orders ops to the second; `i` breaks ties within the same second. Use timestamp_to_ts for a `TIMESTAMPTZ` from `t`. Returns a NULL struct for a NULL input.
rows.vgi.doc_md: BSON Timestamp → `STRUCT(t UINTEGER, i UINTEGER)`: the raw (seconds, increment) pair.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Read the (t, i) parts of a Timestamp.","sql":"SELECT (bson.main.timestamp_parts({'t': 1416994483, 'i': 2})).i AS inc"}]
rows.vgi.title: BSON Timestamp Parts

rows: Convert a BSON Timestamp STRUCT(t,i) to a TIMESTAMPTZ (from `t`)

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Convert a BSON internal Timestamp (the decoded `STRUCT(t, i)` replication clock) to a second-resolution `TIMESTAMPTZ` from its `t` (seconds-since-epoch) component — the oplog ordering clock. NOTE this is the MongoDB-internal 0x11 Timestamp, NOT the user-facing 0x09 UTCDateTime: a 0x11 value is a replication marker, not a wall-clock time. Returns NULL when the input struct has no integer `t`.
rows.vgi.doc_md: BSON Timestamp `STRUCT(t,i)` → `TIMESTAMPTZ` from the `t` seconds (the oplog clock).
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Convert a Timestamp struct to a TIMESTAMPTZ.","sql":"SELECT bson.main.timestamp_to_ts({'t': 1416994483, 'i': 1}) AS ts"}]
rows.vgi.title: BSON Timestamp → TIMESTAMPTZ

rows: Render a BSON document as canonical Extended JSON v2

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Render a BSON document as MongoDB Extended JSON v2. `mode` is 'canonical' (default — the type-preserving, lossless form that wraps every typed value: {"$oid":…}, {"$numberDecimal":…}, {"$date":{"$numberLong":…}}, {"$timestamp":{t,i}}, {"$binary":{base64,subType}}, {"$minKey":1}) or 'relaxed' (human-readable — in-range numbers and dates render natively, only out-of-range/typed values keep wrappers). Canonical is the migration/diff surface and round-trips byte-identically through from_json. to_json always succeeds on a well-formed document; returns NULL for a malformed blob.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Render BSON as Extended JSON v2. `mode` ∈ {canonical (lossless, default), relaxed (readable)}.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Relaxed Extended JSON of {a:1}.","sql":"SELECT bson.main.to_json(bson.main.from_json('{\"a\":1}'), 'relaxed') AS j"}]
rows.vgi.title: BSON → Extended JSON v2

rows: Return the top-level BSON type name of a document

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Return the BSON type name at a dotted path: 'objectId', 'decimal128', 'timestamp', 'date', 'binData:uuid', 'binData:generic', 'binData:encrypted', 'minKey', 'int', 'long', 'double', 'string', 'object', 'array', … . With no `path` (or NULL) it returns the top-level type ('object'). The binData subtype is surfaced after the colon, so you can tell a `UUID`, an encrypted (FLE) blob, or a generic blob apart. A missing path → NULL. Returns NULL for a malformed blob.
rows.vgi.doc_md: BSON type name at a path, e.g. 'objectId', 'decimal128', 'binData:uuid'. NULL path → top-level 'object'.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Type of a nested ObjectId field.","sql":"SELECT bson.main.type_of(bson.main.from_json('{\"_id\":{\"$oid\":\"54759eb3c090d83494e2d804\"}}'), '_id') AS t"}]
rows.vgi.title: BSON Type Of

rows: Diagnose BSON well-formedness: STRUCT(ok BOOL, error VARCHAR, kind VARCHAR)

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Diagnose a BSON blob and return `STRUCT(ok BOOL, error VARCHAR, kind VARCHAR)`. `kind` is one of truncated, length-mismatch, trailing-bytes, invalid-type, bad-cstring, bad-utf8, duplicate-key, nesting-limit, bad-decimal128, bad-subtype (NULL when ok). Stricter than `is_valid`: it also flags duplicate document keys and trailing bytes. Never errors or panics on hostile input — a lying gigabyte length prefix or a 5000-deep document returns ok=false with the classified reason, so a bad row never crashes the scan.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Diagnose well-formedness → `STRUCT(ok, error, kind)`. `kind` ∈ {truncated, length-mismatch, trailing-bytes, invalid-type, bad-cstring, bad-utf8, duplicate-key, nesting-limit, bad-decimal128, bad-subtype}.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Diagnose a truncated document.","sql":"SELECT (bson.main.well_formed(from_hex('0500000001'))).kind AS kind"}]
rows.vgi.title: BSON Well-Formed Diagnosis
